headline: WALL OVER
*~4 FT* TALL?
beats.vo: Wall over about *four feet*? Check this first.
In many Lower Mainland cities, walls over about four feet need a *permit* and an *engineer*.
Some set the line lower. *Maple Ridge* wants a permit over about *two feet*.

headline: TOO CLOSE =
*ONE TALL WALL*
beats.vo: Two short walls stacked close together act like *one tall wall*, so terraces need *real spacing*.
*Clay soil*, a *driveway above*, and *earthquake country* all mean taller walls get engineered here.

beats.vo: Send this to anyone planning a wall.

post.caption: Planning a retaining wall in the Lower Mainland? In many cities, walls over about 4 ft (1.2 m) need a permit and an engineer, and some set the line lower (Maple Ridge: a permit over 0.6 m). Terraced walls need real spacing, and walls holding up driveways or slopes get engineered. Check your city first.
post.alt: Two-tier terraced block retaining walls along a sidewalk, an animated diagram showing why terraced walls need spacing, and a sloped front yard rebuilt with two tiers of block walls and steps.
